title: My cybersecurity and cloud learning goal

claim_boundary.statement: I am publishing a learning intention and an evidence route. I am not claiming completion, mastery, a credential or professional experience.
claim_boundary.safe_scope: I will use the fictional or dummy evidence and the safe boundaries stated in each lab.
claim_boundary.tool_limit: A matching helper result can check an expected decision or format; it cannot judge my reasoning or prove independent skill.

status_model.planned: I have selected the lab and its prerequisites, but I have not claimed an attempt.
status_model.guided: I have worked with instructions, examples or prompts and recorded that help.
status_model.solo: I have preserved a first answer to a changed case before checking a reference.
status_model.reviewed: A person has challenged my evidence and reasoning, and I have retained the feedback and correction.
status_model.recall: I have tried different facts later without reusing my earlier answer.

review_gate.statement: Before I start a dependent lab, I will keep reviewed or equivalent evidence for each named dependency.
review_gate.unavailable_reviewer: I will mark the work awaiting review and will not call it independently demonstrated.

stages.title: Make bounded decisions
stages.complexity: I will use small fictional records to practise one bounded decision at a time.
stages.mastery_note: This label describes exercise complexity, not my current ability.

evidence.artifact: Scope sheet
evidence.decision: I will name the owner, targets, allowed actions, exclusions, time window, stop conditions and pending approval.

evidence.artifact: I will retain a synthetic packet worksheet with exact frame references and stated capture limits.
evidence.decision: I will match each DNS question to any visible reply by endpoints, ports, DNS ID, name and type; distinguish an A answer, NXDOMAIN and no visible reply; use only the supplied synthetic evidence rather than claim a live capture; and not treat the exercise as proof of packet loss, application success, answer truth, professional use, completion or mastery.

evidence.artifact: I will retain a synthetic DNS cache worksheet that cites each query ID, owner and record type, CNAME path, receipt and query times, TTL or negative-cache lifetime, expiry arithmetic, seconds remaining, predicted answer, uncertainty and next check.
evidence.decision: I will use only the supplied offline records. I will calculate remaining life as `max(0, receipt time + TTL − query time)`, treat zero as refresh-required, require every CNAME and final record in a chain to remain fresh, and use the smaller of SOA TTL and MINIMUM for a negative entry. I will distinguish exact-name NXDOMAIN from type-specific NODATA and treat missing or expired cache evidence as refresh-required, not proof that a name or service is unavailable. I will state that the exercise performs no DNS lookup and does not establish reachability, application success, current resolver state or the truth of a cached answer; record sets, DNSSEC, resolver caps, prefetch, serve-stale and failure caching remain outside scope.

evidence.artifact: Role/resource/action matrix
evidence.decision: I will preserve required access while removing permissions without a stated business need.

evidence.artifact: I will retain a fictional Linux access worksheet citing the actor, groups, canonical paths, owner/group/other mode bits, selected permission class, required target bits, every ancestor search check, result, uncertainty and next check.
evidence.decision: I will use only the supplied synthetic records; select owner bits before group and other without falling back to a more permissive class; require search permission on every ancestor directory; distinguish directory read from search and require write plus search to create an entry. I will treat each result as allowed or denied by this small mode-bit model only; run no chmod or host inspection; mark ACLs, SELinux, capabilities, special bits, symbolic links, mount restrictions and deletion semantics outside scope; and not treat a helper match as proof of real access, system safety, professional use, completion, mastery or independent assessment.

evidence.artifact: I will retain a fictional SSH configuration review citing the exact config lines, first effective value for each of six supported directives, ignored duplicates, baseline label, authentication-route result, uncertainty and next verification check.
evidence.decision: I will use only supplied synthetic text; accept plain keyword/value pairs for the lab’s six directives; apply the first-value rule; keep missing settings unknown rather than assume version defaults; compare explicit values only with the fictional baseline; and distinguish a supported method from a working login. I will reject Match, Include, unknown directives and complex syntax; read or change no host configuration; run no server, command or network test; state that keys, PAM, exposure and recovery remain unchecked; and not treat a helper match as proof of secure configuration, usable access, professional use, completion, mastery or independent assessment.

evidence.artifact: Sorted sign-in timeline and handover
evidence.decision: I will separate rule matches, interpretation and the next evidence request.

evidence.artifact: UTC event timeline
evidence.decision: I will cite exact event records and state uncertainty in a short handover.

evidence.artifact: Labelled packet-path diagram and worksheet
evidence.decision: I will show route matches, the selected next hop and what the path cannot prove.

evidence.artifact: TCP flow table with exact frame references and sequence/acknowledgement calculations
evidence.decision: I will use the supplied synthetic packet summaries to distinguish an observed handshake, reset, no visible response, missing final ACK, missing initial SYN and acknowledgement mismatch; cite exact frames and show sequence/acknowledgement calculations; and state that the excerpt cannot establish full connection state or root cause, that missing packets do not prove packet loss, firewall failure or server fault, that an observed handshake does not prove application success, and that matching helper results do not prove professional use, completion or mastery.

evidence.artifact: I will retain a saved-scan-to-inventory table with exact IP address, TCP port and XML references.
evidence.decision: I will compare the supplied synthetic scan snapshot with the approved inventory; distinguish hosts not present, recorded down or unregistered and expected, missing or unexpected open TCP services; and state that the offline helper does not run a scan. I will not treat one saved snapshot or a matching result as proof of ownership, vulnerability, malicious activity, current state, complete coverage, professional use, completion or mastery.

evidence.artifact: I will retain a fictional finding-priority queue with exact record and field references, impact, exposure, evidence-of-use, service-importance and confidence inputs, each four-part score, any overriding rule, uncertainty and the next owner check.
evidence.decision: I will apply only the supplied local rubric to supplied fictional findings: unverified evidence becomes investigate; supplied fictional observed-exploitation records become urgent; otherwise I will assign urgent, planned or routine by score. I will state that the rubric is not CVSS, queue labels do not set deadlines, proof of concept does not prove exploitation, and helper matches do not prove a real vulnerability, real exploitation or current risk, professional use, completion or mastery.

evidence.artifact: I will retain a fictional retest record citing the exact before-and-after record and fields for target, port, method, role, time, observed result and positive-control result, plus my decision, evidence references, limit and next check.
evidence.decision: I will use only supplied synthetic offline records; require a vulnerable baseline with a passed control; compare target case-insensitively and port, method and role exactly; and call a later test not-testable when conditions changed, it was blocked or the control failed, otherwise unchanged or fixed by whether the finding was reproduced. I will state that the helper trusts the supplied observation and control fields, and that fixed covers only those conditions—not general safety or removal of every cause. I will send no traffic or change a system and will not treat a match as proof of a real fix, professional use, completion, mastery or independent assessment.

evidence.artifact: I will retain a fictional component/advisory worksheet citing component IDs, package names, versions, scope, path evidence, advisory IDs, affected-range comparisons, uncertainty and the next check.
evidence.decision: I will compare each supplied stable three-part version numerically with every supplied exact-package [introduced,fixed) range; distinguish no supplied advisory from outside supplied ranges; and separate build exposure from reachable, not-demonstrated and unknown runtime paths. I will state that this offline exercise trusts the supplied inventory and path evidence and does not install packages, fetch live notices, resolve a full dependency chain, model ecosystem-specific version rules or test an exploit. Version, range and helper results do not prove exploitability, safety, professional use, completion or mastery.

evidence.artifact: First-match rule trace
evidence.decision: I will record required traffic kept, excess traffic removed and the model limits.

evidence.artifact: HTTP triage report and evidence note
evidence.decision: I will separate observed requests, possible explanations and the next check.

evidence.artifact: Baseline comparison report
evidence.decision: I will classify exact changes as approved, unexpected or unsupported by the baseline.

evidence.artifact: Backup copy-selection worksheet
evidence.decision: I will use retention, required scope, byte hashes and RPO, then state the check's limits.

evidence.artifact: Storage exposure-path worksheet
evidence.decision: I will cite record IDs, preserve my first prediction and name the next unanswered check.

evidence.artifact: Joiner/mover/leaver access worksheet
evidence.decision: I will explain each keep, remove or review decision from the supplied evidence.

stages.title: Connect controls and evidence
stages.complexity: I will combine earlier reasoning across cloud, identity, network, telemetry and recovery records.
stages.mastery_note: This label describes exercise complexity, not my current ability.

evidence.artifact: I will retain a synthetic account-control worksheet with exact evidence references and stated limits.
evidence.decision: I will compare supplied enrolment, enforcement, recovery, ownership, monitoring and emergency-access records with the lab rules, then state that the helper does not test a real sign-in or prove control effectiveness.

evidence.artifact: Cloud audit-event timeline and handover
evidence.decision: I will distinguish successful actions, denied attempts, coverage gaps and attribution limits.

evidence.artifact: Service/task responsibility table
evidence.decision: I will name the responsible party, agreement evidence, control record, gap and next owner.

evidence.artifact: I will retain a synthetic cloud-resource lifecycle worksheet citing exact resource IDs, owners, expiry and review flags, dependency arrows, retention holds, proposed teardown order, made-up residual daily cost units, budget-alert state, the approver needed for each proposed step and a later bill check.
evidence.decision: I will use only supplied offline records; identify missing ownership or expiry data; block proposed removal when a retention hold or remaining dependency applies; and distinguish review or expiry from deletion approval, a budget alert from a spending cap, and a model-valid order or zero model cost from real deletion or stopped charges. I will run no cloud deletion commands and will not treat the exercise as proof of complete inventory, real removal, stopped spending, professional use, completion or mastery.

evidence.artifact: Request/statement decision table
evidence.decision: I will distinguish allow, explicit deny and implicit deny and compare one copied policy change.

evidence.artifact: Human-to-role-to-session timeline
evidence.decision: I will trace issue, expiry, revocation and action decisions without overclaiming attribution.

evidence.artifact: Two-leg cloud path diagram and reachability table
evidence.decision: I will trace addressing, route choice, inbound rules and untested assumptions.

evidence.artifact: Import report, rejected-record list and reconciliation note
evidence.decision: I will link normalised and rejected rows back to their source evidence.

evidence.artifact: Telemetry coverage timeline
evidence.decision: I will show expected records, arrival times, heartbeat evidence, gaps and the smallest next check.

evidence.artifact: Dummy-data restore receipt
evidence.decision: I will compare copied and verified hashes, measured durations and the restored version with the baseline.

evidence.artifact: Dummy-file evidence register and copy receipt
evidence.decision: I will link each copy to its recorded source, compare source and copy hashes, record UTC handling gaps and state what those records cannot prove.

evidence.artifact: I will retain a DEMO-only secret exposure worksheet and evidence note.
evidence.decision: I will trace only exact listed markers through configuration, saved changes and logs, distinguish active and revoked values, keep response proposals bounded and state what the supplied files cannot prove.

evidence.artifact: I will retain a fictional data-handling register citing exact record and field references, owner and purpose, fields to keep or leave out, handling label, storage and reader rules, retention and hold state, sharing decision, one proposed exception, and the stated scope of each disposal receipt.
evidence.decision: I will apply only supplied synthetic records and invented local rules; treat a hold as overriding age; distinguish disposal due from authorised and verified deletion, and listed-copy coverage from erasure; mark absent authority, date, method and checks as not supplied; and label exceptions proposed, not approved. I will state that the helper trusts the structured disposal field rather than verifying receipt prose. I will perform no deletion, sharing or live test and will not treat results as legal advice or proof of real deletion, control effectiveness, professional use, completion or mastery.

stages.title: Build and communicate a case
stages.complexity: I will connect several evidence types while keeping alternative explanations, authority and audience boundaries visible.
stages.mastery_note: This label describes exercise complexity, not my current ability.

evidence.artifact: I will retain a fictional GRC decision pack containing written scope, a risk register with exact evidence IDs, a control-evidence matrix, a pending exception record, a challenge log and a sanitized decision report.
evidence.decision: I will apply only the lab’s local 1–3 teaching rubric to the supplied fictional case; separate events and plausible harms from confirmed facts; distinguish proposed controls and projected residual risk from checked operation; keep acceptance pending when authority, threshold, obligation or approval is not supplied; and record the owner, review date, uncertainty and bounded next check. I will perform no live action and will not treat helper matches, a worked reference or framework mapping as proof of a real incident, control effectiveness, legal compliance, professional use, completion, mastery or independent assessment.

evidence.artifact: Process tree and bounded handover
evidence.decision: I will cite parent, location, signature and change context without asserting malware.

evidence.artifact: Deduplicated and correlated alert set
evidence.decision: I will state the time-window rule and avoid treating alert counts as incident counts.

evidence.artifact: Saved SQL and expected/actual result tables
evidence.decision: I will reconcile distinct-event counts and explain any join multiplication.

evidence.artifact: Four-part incident case notebook
evidence.decision: I will build a timeline, two hypotheses, evidence needs and a bounded handover.

evidence.artifact: Containment decision table
evidence.decision: I will name authority, operational effect, evidence preservation, owner and release check.

evidence.artifact: Staff message, technical handover and manager update
evidence.decision: I will separate confirmed facts, hypotheses, gaps, actions and owners for each audience.
